How It Works
Search Resource

This network is a literature-based search resource. Type any molecule, hormone, or protein name into the search bar to instantly highlight all organ–organ connections where that molecule was identified as a key player in the retrieved literature.

Example Searches
  • bile acid — connections involving bile acid crosstalk
  • glucose — all axes where glucose metabolism is reported
  • insulin — edges where insulin signalling plays a role
  • GLP-1 — incretin-mediated inter-organ communication
  • AMPK — energy-sensing kinase across organ axes
  • FGF21 — hepatokine crosstalk connections
Key Player Categories
  • Hormones — secreted signalling molecules: insulin, glucagon, leptin, GLP-1, cortisol, irisin, adiponectin, …
  • Metabolites — small molecules: glucose, lactate, fatty acids, bile acids, ketone bodies, amino acids, TCA intermediates, …
  • Proteins — enzymes, transporters, receptors: GLUT1–5, AMPK, mTOR, PPARs, PGC-1α, FGF21, LPL, CPT1, …
Threshold Filter

Use the Key Players button to set a minimum mention count. Only molecules mentioned at least that many times across all retrieved abstracts for an edge will be shown as chips and matched by search. This helps surface the most consistently reported signals.

Coverage

All 91 possible organ–organ pairs from 14 organs were searched regardless of any prior anatomical assumptions. An edge is drawn only when the literature returns ≥10 papers for that pair.

Query Structure

For each pair A–B, the primary PubMed query is:

(MeSH_A OR organ_A_aliases) AND (MeSH_B OR organ_B_aliases) AND (metabolism OR metabolic OR substrate OR glucose OR "fatty acid" OR insulin OR energy OR oxidation OR hormone)

If this returns fewer than 5 papers, a cascade fallback removes the metabolic keyword filter and searches by organ names + date only. The strategy used is shown in the edge sidebar.

Key Player Extraction

All retrieved abstracts are scanned against three curated vocabulary lists (hormones, metabolites, proteins). Each term match across all abstracts for an edge is counted and ranked. These counts drive the chip display and search.
